question: Excluding stoppages, the speed of a bus is 60 km/h and including stoppages, it is 42 km/h. For how many minute does the bus stop per hour?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Direct formula for stoppage time per hour:

Stoppage time = [(Faster Speed − Slower Speed) ÷ Faster Speed] × 60 minutes

Stoppage time = [(60 − 42) ÷ 60] × 60

Stoppage time = (18 ÷ 60) × 60 = 18 minutes

**∴ The correct answer is 18 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f40ffa92fe01c310ae1df00b8e279247a7b54615d0fddb7ae77b2052b4831398.png] 

**Given:**

Speed without stoppages = 60 km/h

Speed with stoppages = 42 km/h

**Formula Used:**

Stoppage time per hour = Distance not covered due to stoppages ÷ Speed without stoppages

**Calculations:**

⇒ Distance covered in 1 hour without stoppage = 60 km

⇒ Distance actually covered in 1 hour with stoppage = 42 km

⇒ Loss in distance due to stoppage = 60 − 42 = 18 km

⇒ Time required to cover this 18 km at the normal speed of 60 km/h represents the total stoppage time.

⇒ Time = Distance ÷ Speed

⇒ Stoppage time = 18 ÷ 60 hours

⇒ To convert into minutes, multiply by 60.

⇒ Stoppage time = (18 ÷ 60) × 60 = 18 minutes

**∴ The correct answer is 18 minutes.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Average Speed with Stoppages

It is the total distance traveled divided by the total time taken, including both driving time and the time the vehicle was stationary.

Average Speed without Stoppages

It is the total distance traveled divided by the actual driving time only, completely ignoring any stopping periods.

Direct Formula for Stoppage Time

Stoppage time per hour = (Faster speed − Slower speed) ÷ Faster speed. To get the time in minutes, simply multiply the fraction by 60.
